theme: The child born to us; the shoot of Jesse; peaceable kingdom
readingInstruction: Read Isaiah 9:1-12:6. These chapters contain the great Messianic promises of Isaiah: the child born to us, the shoot from the stump of Jesse, and the peaceable kingdom. Read them as light dawning in a dark place.
settingTheScene: Chapter 8 ended in darkness and distress, with a people who consult mediums and find only gloom. Chapter 9 begins with a “but.” The land of Zebulun and Naphtali, the first to be devastated by Assyria, will be the first to see light. In these chapters, Isaiah gives his most famous portrait of the coming king, and promises that after the Assyrian axe comes a shoot from the stump of David’s family.
observation: “The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; those who dwelt in a land of deep darkness, on them has light shone” (9:2).
“For to us a child is born, to us a son is given; and the government shall be upon his shoulder” (9:6).
“And his name shall be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace” (9:6).
“Of the increase of his government and of peace there will be no end” (9:7).
“For all this his anger has not turned away, and his hand is stretched out still” (9:12).
“There shall come forth a shoot from the stump of Jesse, and a branch from his roots shall bear fruit” (11:1).
“The Spirit of the LORD shall rest upon him, the Spirit of wisdom and understanding” (11:2).
“The wolf shall dwell with the lamb… for the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea” (11:6, 9).
interpretation:
The light in chapter 9 is a reversal. Isaiah says the very place that first suffered under Assyria will be honored. Galilee, a region in the far north that was despised, becomes the setting for the good news. The prophecy then explains why: a child is born. The one who comes is a human child, born into the line of David, and yet his names point beyond the human. “Mighty God” and “Everlasting Father” are titles that no merely human king could carry. “Wonderful Counselor” means that he needs no advice, and “Prince of Peace” means that he brings wholeness. His government will have no end, and it will rest on justice and righteousness.

Notice the phrase, “The zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this.” God himself is committed to accomplishing it. Yet the rest of chapter 9 and chapter 10 describe the judgment that comes first. Assyria is God’s axe, used to chop down his own people, but then judged for its pride. The tool that boasts against its maker will be broken. “Shall the axe boast over him who hews with it?”

Chapter 11 returns to hope. The Assyrian army is described as a forest cut down, but a shoot comes from the stump of Jesse. The picture is of a royal family reduced to a stump after the fall of David’s line, and yet life springs from it. Upon him rests the Spirit in sevenfold fullness. He judges the poor with righteousness. And his reign restores creation itself: the wolf with the lamb, the leopard with the young goat, a child leading them. The cause is that “the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.”

Chapter 12 ends the section with a song. “Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and will not be afraid.” “With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.” The proper response to such promises is song.
connection: Matthew 4:12-16 quotes Isaiah 9:1-2 and says that Jesus began his ministry in Galilee. Luke 1:32-33 echoes Isaiah 9:7 in the angel’s announcement to Mary. Revelation 5:5 calls Jesus the Root of David, and Romans 15:12 quotes Isaiah 11:10. At his baptism the Spirit rested on Jesus (Matthew 3:16). Romans 8:19-21 speaks of creation itself being set free. John 7:37-38 recalls the wells of salvation.
application:
Read Isaiah 9:6 aloud and pause on each of the four names. Which one do you most need today?

Think about a dark place in your life or community. Pray for light to shine there.

Sing or read Isaiah 12:2 as a prayer of trust.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for the light that has dawned on you.
Praise the child as Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
Ask him to bring his peace where you are.
